actions.name: Register signers and thresholds on a Stellar account
actions.summary: The holder of an existing funded Stellar account makes it a weighted multisig: one transaction of SetOptions operations adds each member's ed25519 key with a weight and sets the master weight and the low, medium and high thresholds. The rule then lives in the account entry, and the protocol checks it on every later transaction.

fields.name: account
fields.means: the existing, funded Stellar account (G… address) that becomes the multisig

fields.name: signers
fields.means: the signers to add: each a member-disclosed ed25519 public key with a weight from 1 to 255, one SetOptions operation per signer

fields.name: masterWeight
fields.means: the new weight of the account's own master key (0 turns it off)

fields.name: low
fields.means: the LOW threshold, 0-255 (BumpSequence, and the transaction itself)

fields.name: med
fields.means: the MEDIUM threshold, 0-255 (payments, contract calls, most operations)

fields.name: high
fields.means: the HIGH threshold, 0-255 (changing signers or thresholds, merging the account)

fields.name: fee
fields.means: the maximum total fee in stroops, paid by the account (at least 100 stroops per operation)

fields.name: seqNum
fields.means: the account's sequence number + 1, read from the chain

fields.name: maxTime
fields.means: the timeBounds upper limit in UNIX seconds; after it the transaction is invalid (0 = never)

agreement.threshold: signatures whose weights sum to at least the account's current HIGH threshold (a fresh account: its master key, weight 1, against threshold 0)

requirements.name: stellar:*
requirements.target: stellar:*

requirements.name: stellar-rpc
requirements.target: stellar:* (account reads, transaction submit)

requirements.name: stellar-signer-key
requirements.target: stellar-account:<G… multisig account> (ed25519 signer; weight toward HIGH)

requirements.name: signer-keys
requirements.target: stellar-account:<G… multisig account> signers (ed25519, disclosed by each holder, weight 1-255, at most 20)

requirements.name: xlm-for-reserve
requirements.target: stellar-account:<G… multisig account> (0.5 XLM base reserve per added signer, plus the fee)

steps.does: Writes the effect: the keys and weights members disclosed, the master weight and the three thresholds. Muster would read the account's balance, sequence number and current signers from the RPC, record each read, build one SetOptions operation per signer, re-derive the transaction hash, and check the result: every threshold at most the total weight that remains.

Each current signer (for a fresh account, the master key alone) rebuilds the transaction, checks the hash, and signs. SetOptions that touches signers or thresholds is a HIGH-threshold operation, checked against the account as it was before any operation applies.
steps.signs: Ed25519, by each signer's key, over the 32-byte transaction hash SHA-256(XDR(TransactionSignaturePayload{networkId = SHA-256(network passphrase, e.g. "Public Global Stellar Network ; September 2015"), taggedTransaction = ENVELOPE_TYPE_TX (2) + Transaction{sourceAccount = the multisig account, fee = uint32 maximum total fee in stroops, seqNum = the account's sequence number + 1, cond = preconditions (timeBounds minTime/maxTime; muster would set maxTime to the room's expiry), memo, operations = [SetOptions{signer = {key: SIGNER_KEY_TYPE_ED25519, weight}} per signer; the first also sets masterWeight, lowThreshold, medThreshold, highThreshold], ext = 0}})). Inside: the network id, the account, the sequence number, the fee and the time bounds. Not inside: any other signature. Attached as a DecoratedSignature: a 4-byte hint (the last 4 bytes of the signer's public key) and the 64-byte signature.

steps.does: One member attaches the collected signatures (at most 20) to the envelope and submits it through the RPC. The RPC provider sees the signed transaction first; validators see it before it is in a ledger. The account pays the fee.

The ledger closes. From here the account entry lists every signer key, its weight and the thresholds, readable by anyone. Muster would read the account back, record the read, and check it matches the effect.

refusals.what: an approval over a transaction hash that differs from the one the room re-derived from the reviewed effect
refusals.why: invariant 1 / F-4: effects are reviewed, the transaction hash is the materialization, and a mismatch refuses

refusals.what: signing a payload whose networkId is not SHA-256 of the room's network passphrase, or whose source account or sequence number differs from the effect
refusals.why: invariant 2: the payload must commit to environment, account and slot. Stellar binds explicitly: the network id is inside the signed hash, and a signature made for another network fails txBAD_AUTH

refusals.what: a resulting configuration in which any threshold exceeds the total weight of the signers that remain (including a master weight of 0 with too little weight left)
refusals.why: the chain does not check it: SetOptions writes weights and thresholds as given, and a threshold above the total weight can never be met again, so the account is locked for that operation class

refusals.what: more than 20 signers on the account, a weight or threshold above 255, or the account's own master key as an added signer
refusals.why: the chain's rule: SET_OPTIONS_TOO_MANY_SIGNERS, SET_OPTIONS_THRESHOLD_OUT_OF_RANGE and SET_OPTIONS_BAD_SIGNER

refusals.what: adding signers when the account's available balance cannot cover one more base reserve (0.5 XLM) per new signer plus the fee
refusals.why: the chain's rule: each signer is a subentry that raises the minimum balance; otherwise SET_OPTIONS_LOW_RESERVE

refusals.what: adding a signer that is not an ed25519 key held by a named member: a pre-authorized transaction hash, a hash(x), or an ed25519 signed-payload signer
refusals.why: invariant 9: every driver is named. These signer types authorize without a keyholder's live approval: a pre-auth hash authorizes one exact transaction, anyone who learns x can use a hash(x) signer, and a signed-payload signature is checked against its fixed payload, not the transaction

refusals.what: attaching a signature the protocol would not need: the collected weights must reach the HIGH threshold only with the last signature attached, in envelope order
refusals.why: the chain's rule: the checker walks the signatures in order and stops once the weight meets the threshold; any signature it never used fails the whole transaction with txBAD_AUTH_EXTRA, so collection must stop at exactly enough

refusals.what: collecting on, or submitting, a transaction whose seqNum is no longer the account's sequence number + 1 (another transaction from the account landed first)
refusals.why: the chain's rule: the sequence number must be exactly one above the account's (txBAD_SEQ); muster would re-read the account before submit and mark the proposal stale

refusals.what: collecting after the room's expiry, or submitting after the transaction's timeBounds.maxTime
refusals.why: invariant 2 (expiry) and the chain's rule: after maxTime the transaction fails txTOO_LATE; with maxTime 0 a signed transaction never expires on its own

refusals.what: signing when a read that reached the signed bytes (the sequence number, balance, current signers and fee) is not recorded in the room log as an external read
refusals.why: invariant 10: nothing is signed whose inputs cannot be accounted for; the sequence number and fee come from the chain, not the room

claims.claim: The signed bytes name the network: networkId = SHA-256(passphrase) is inside every signature payload, so a signature is worthless on another Stellar network.
After setup the protocol itself checks the signers' weights against the thresholds for every transaction from the account.
The policy is public from setup: every signer key, weight and threshold is in the account entry.
The chain accepts a threshold above the total signer weight, which locks the account; only a client-side check would stop it.
claims.party: the signers who approve a setup outside muster

claims.claim: Pre-authorized transaction and hash(x) signers can be added to the account and then authorize without the keyholders; muster would not register them through this action.
claims.party: whoever registered the pre-authorized transaction hash, or anyone who learns x (public once it is used)

evidence.what: TransactionSignaturePayload = {networkId, taggedTransaction = ENVELOPE_TYPE_TX + Transaction}: the bytes every signer's key signs (after SHA-256).
Transaction = {sourceAccount, fee, seqNum, cond (preconditions), memo, operations, ext (Soroban data)}: everything a signature commits to.
DecoratedSignature = {hint: last 4 bytes of the public key, signature}; TransactionV1Envelope carries signatures<20>.
stellar-core: the contents hash is sha256(xdr(networkID, ENVELOPE_TYPE_TX, tx)) and every signature is checked against it.
stellar-core: networkID = sha256(NETWORK_PASSPHRASE), so the network is inside every signed hash.
js-stellar-base: the network passphrases (public, testnet, futurenet, standalone) whose SHA-256 is the networkId.

stellar-core SignatureChecker: pre-auth-tx signers match the contents hash with no signature; hash(x) signers match sha256(signature); ed25519 signatures are walked in envelope order until the weight meets the needed threshold.
stellar-core: checkAllSignaturesUsed fails when any attached signature was never needed.
stellar-core: an unused signature fails the transaction with txBAD_AUTH_EXTRA.
stellar-core checkAllTransactionSignatures: the transaction's source account must meet its LOW threshold (and any extraSigners).
stellar-core OperationFrame::checkSignature: each operation's source account must meet that operation's threshold, else opBAD_AUTH.
stellar-core isBadSeq: without minSeqNum the tx seqNum must be exactly account seq + 1; with minSeqNum it is valid while minSeqNum <= account seq < tx seqNum.
Result codes: txTOO_LATE (after maxTime), txBAD_SEQ, txBAD_AUTH (too few valid signatures / wrong network), txBAD_AUTH_EXTRA (unused signatures).
AccountEntry holds seqNum, thresholds [master weight | low | med | high] and signers<20>: the policy is ledger state anyone can read.
Stellar docs: thresholds 0-255 per low/medium/high class, up to 20 signatures per transaction, leftover signatures fail with TX_BAD_AUTH_EXTRA, pre-authorized transaction and hash(x) signer types.

Stellar docs: sequence number must be account seq + 1 unless preconditions relax it; preconditions (time bounds, ledger bounds, minSeqNum, minSeqAge, minSeqLedgerGap, extraSigners); the network passphrase is part of the signed hash.
SEP-7 web+stellar:tx URI: a TransactionEnvelope handed to a signer's wallet, with pubkey and callback for multisig coordination; the family's interop format.
Refractor: a hosted multisig aggregator and pending-transaction store for Stellar; the server the room replaces (invariant 8).
stellar-core SetOptionsOpFrame: any change to masterWeight, a threshold, or a signer is a HIGH-threshold operation; otherwise MEDIUM.
stellar-core SetOptions doApply: writes weights and thresholds as given, with no check that the thresholds stay reachable; weight 0 deletes a signer.
stellar-core SetOptions doCheckValid: weights and thresholds above 255 and the account's own key as signer are refused.
MAX_SIGNERS = 20.
Stellar docs: base reserve 0.5 XLM; minimum balance is 2 base reserves plus one per subentry, and signers are subentries.
Stellar docs, list of operations: Set Options is HIGH when it changes signers or thresholds; SET_OPTIONS_TOO_MANY_SIGNERS, SET_OPTIONS_LOW_RESERVE, SET_OPTIONS_BAD_SIGNER.
stellar-core processSignatures: every operation's signatures are checked before any operation applies.
CAP-40: the ed25519 signed-payload signer type, a signature over a fixed payload rather than the transaction.

unverified: The Stellar docs warn only that a master weight of 0 can lock the account; the general lockout (any threshold above the total remaining weight) is derived from the authorization rule and SetOptions applying without a check, not stated in the docs.

actions.name: Send XLM from a Stellar multisig account
actions.summary: Members of a weighted multisig account send native XLM. Each signer signs the same transaction hash in the room until the weights reach the account's medium threshold; one member submits, and the account pays the fee. The protocol checks the rule.

fields.name: account
fields.means: the multisig account paying (the transaction and operation source)

fields.name: to
fields.means: the payee's Stellar account (G… or muxed M… address); it must already exist

fields.name: amount
fields.means: the XLM amount in stroops (int64; 1 XLM = 10,000,000 stroops)

fields.name: memo
fields.means: the transaction memo, public on the ledger (none, text, id, hash or return)

fields.name: fee
fields.means: the maximum total fee in stroops, paid by the account (at least 100 stroops per operation)

fields.name: seqNum
fields.means: the account's sequence number + 1, read from the chain; it orders this payment after the account's earlier transactions

fields.name: maxTime
fields.means: the timeBounds upper limit in UNIX seconds; after it the transaction is invalid (0 = never)

agreement.threshold: signatures whose weights sum to at least the account's MEDIUM threshold (and its LOW threshold for the transaction itself); at most 20 signatures

requirements.name: stellar:*
requirements.target: stellar:*

requirements.name: stellar-rpc
requirements.target: stellar:* (account reads, transaction submit)

requirements.name: stellar-signer-key
requirements.target: stellar-account:<G… multisig account> (ed25519 signer; weight toward MEDIUM)

requirements.name: payee
requirements.target: stellar-account:<G… payee> (must already exist)

requirements.name: xlm-available
requirements.target: stellar-account:<G… multisig account> (balance - minimum balance - selling liabilities >= amount + fee)

steps.does: Writes the payee, the amount, a memo and an expiry. Muster would read the account's sequence number and balance and check that the payee exists, record each read, build the transaction and re-derive its hash. The proposal takes the next sequence number: it settles after the account's earlier transactions, and any other transaction from the account that lands first makes it stale.
Each signer's client rebuilds the transaction from the effect, checks the hash, and signs. Payment is a MEDIUM-threshold operation. Muster would stop at exactly enough weight.
steps.signs: Ed25519, by each signer's key, over the 32-byte transaction hash SHA-256(XDR(TransactionSignaturePayload{networkId = SHA-256(network passphrase, e.g. "Public Global Stellar Network ; September 2015"), taggedTransaction = ENVELOPE_TYPE_TX (2) + Transaction{sourceAccount = the multisig account, fee = uint32 maximum total fee in stroops, seqNum = the account's sequence number + 1, cond = preconditions (timeBounds minTime/maxTime; muster would set maxTime to the room's expiry), memo, operations = [Payment{destination = to, asset = native, amount}], ext = 0}})). Inside: the network id, the account, the sequence number, the fee and the time bounds. Not inside: any other signature. Attached as a DecoratedSignature: a 4-byte hint (the last 4 bytes of the signer's public key) and the 64-byte signature.

steps.does: One member attaches the signatures (at most 20) and submits through the RPC. The RPC provider sees the signed transaction first; validators see it before it is in a ledger. The protocol checks LOW weight for the transaction, MEDIUM for the payment, the sequence number and the time bounds. The account pays the fee, even if the transaction fails once applied. A fee-bump wrapper, signed separately by another account, would move the fee to that account.
The ledger closes. The payer, payee, amount, memo and every signature's hint stay in the public ledger. Muster would read the result, record it, and fold it into the room's view.

actions.name: Call a Soroban contract from a Stellar multisig account
actions.summary: Members of a weighted multisig account invoke a Soroban contract. With the account as the transaction source, its authorization rides on the envelope signatures, which must reach the medium threshold. If someone else submits, the account authorizes through an address-credential entry: its signers sign a separate Soroban payload, and the host checks the same medium threshold.

fields.name: account
fields.means: the multisig account authorizing the call (by default also the transaction source and fee payer)

fields.name: contract
fields.means: the Soroban contract address (C…) being invoked

fields.name: function
fields.means: the contract function name (SCSymbol)

fields.name: args
fields.means: the call's arguments (SCVal list)

fields.name: auth
fields.means: the SorobanAuthorizationEntry list: source-account credentials for this account when it is the transaction source; address credentials V2 otherwise

fields.name: sorobanData
fields.means: the footprint, resource limits and resourceFee returned by simulation (the transaction's ext)

fields.name: authNonce
fields.means: address credentials only: the int64 nonce the host consumes for this account

fields.name: signatureExpirationLedger
fields.means: address credentials only: the last ledger at which the auth signatures are valid

fields.name: fee
fields.means: the maximum total fee in stroops: the resource fee plus the inclusion fee, paid by the transaction source

fields.name: seqNum
fields.means: the transaction source's sequence number + 1, read from the chain

fields.name: maxTime
fields.means: the timeBounds upper limit in UNIX seconds (0 = never)

agreement.threshold: signatures whose weights sum to at least the account's MEDIUM threshold, both for the envelope and for an address-credential auth entry

requirements.name: stellar:*
requirements.target: stellar:*

requirements.name: stellar-rpc
requirements.target: stellar:* (account reads, transaction submit)

requirements.name: stellar-rpc-simulate
requirements.target: stellar:* simulateTransaction (footprint, resource fee, auth entries)

requirements.name: stellar-signer-key
requirements.target: stellar-account:<G… multisig account> (ed25519 signer; weight toward MEDIUM)

requirements.name: contract
requirements.target: stellar-contract:<C… contract> (instance and code live on the ledger)

requirements.name: xlm-for-fee
requirements.target: stellar-account:<G… multisig account> (resource fee + inclusion fee, above the minimum balance)

steps.does: Writes the contract, function and arguments. Muster would send the unsigned transaction to the RPC's simulateTransaction, which returns the footprint, the resource fee and the auth entries; it would record that result as an external read, check that the auth entries name only this account and the reviewed invocation, and re-derive the transaction hash. Simulation shows the whole call to the RPC provider before anyone signs. In recording mode the host meters one signature for an address-credential account, so a multisig entry may need more budget than simulated.

Each signer rebuilds the transaction and signs its hash. With the account as the transaction source, its auth entry uses source-account credentials: the host accepts the envelope's signatures as the account's authorization, and the protocol checks them against MEDIUM for the InvokeHostFunction operation. With address credentials, each signer also signs the Soroban payload, and the host checks that those keys' weights reach MEDIUM. The driver, not the core, reads the auth entries and the signature vector (invariant 6). Muster would stop at exactly enough weight on the envelope.
steps.signs: Ed25519, by each signer's key, over the 32-byte transaction hash SHA-256(XDR(TransactionSignaturePayload{networkId = SHA-256(network passphrase, e.g. "Public Global Stellar Network ; September 2015"), taggedTransaction = ENVELOPE_TYPE_TX (2) + Transaction{sourceAccount = the multisig account, fee = uint32 maximum total fee in stroops, seqNum = the account's sequence number + 1, cond = preconditions (timeBounds minTime/maxTime; muster would set maxTime to the room's expiry), memo, operations = [InvokeHostFunction{hostFunction = invokeContract{contract, function, args}, auth = [SorobanAuthorizationEntry{credentials = SOROBAN_CREDENTIALS_SOURCE_ACCOUNT, rootInvocation}]} (a Soroban transaction holds one operation)], ext = 1: SorobanTransactionData{resources = {footprint, instructions, diskReadBytes, writeBytes}, resourceFee}}})). Inside: the network id, the account, the sequence number, the fee and the time bounds. Not inside: any other signature. Attached as a DecoratedSignature: a 4-byte hint (the last 4 bytes of the signer's public key) and the 64-byte signature. With address credentials instead: each signer also signs, with Ed25519, SHA-256(XDR(HashIDPreimage ENVELOPE_TYPE_SOROBAN_AUTHORIZATION_WITH_ADDRESS{networkID, nonce, signatureExpirationLedger, address = the account, invocation})); the legacy ENVELOPE_TYPE_SOROBAN_AUTHORIZATION{networkID, nonce, signatureExpirationLedger, invocation} leaves the address out. Those signatures go into the entry as a vector of {public_key, signature}, strictly ascending by key, and the entry becomes part of the transaction the envelope signers then sign.

steps.does: One member attaches the signatures and submits through the RPC. The RPC provider sees the signed transaction first; validators see the call, its arguments and its footprint before it is in a ledger. The host consumes an address-credential nonce and refuses an expired one. The transaction source pays the resource fee and the inclusion fee.
The ledger closes. The call, its result, its events and the state it changed are public. Muster would read the result, record it, and fold it into the room's view.

actions.name: Change the signers or thresholds of a Stellar multisig account
actions.summary: Members change who can sign, in place: SetOptions operations add, remove (weight 0) or re-weight signers and change the thresholds, and the account address stays. The signers before the change must reach the HIGH threshold; the new set governs from the next transaction.

fields.means: optional: the new master key weight (0 turns it off)

fields.means: optional: the new HIGH threshold, 0-255

steps.does: Writes the change. Muster would read the account's current signers, thresholds, balance and sequence number, record each read, compute the resulting configuration and re-derive the hash. It shows two sets apart: room members, who can read, and account signers, who can authorize. This action admits no one to the room, and a member admitted later reads only from their epoch on.

Each current signer rebuilds the transaction, checks the hash, and signs. The protocol checks every operation's signatures against the account as it was before any operation applies, so the old set authorizes the change. Muster would stop at exactly enough weight.
steps.signs: Ed25519, by each signer's key, over the 32-byte transaction hash SHA-256(XDR(TransactionSignaturePayload{networkId = SHA-256(network passphrase, e.g. "Public Global Stellar Network ; September 2015"), taggedTransaction = ENVELOPE_TYPE_TX (2) + Transaction{sourceAccount = the multisig account, fee = uint32 maximum total fee in stroops, seqNum = the account's sequence number + 1, cond = preconditions (timeBounds minTime/maxTime; muster would set maxTime to the room's expiry), memo, operations = [SetOptions{signer = {key, weight}} per added or re-weighted signer, SetOptions{signer = {key, weight = 0}} per removed signer, and SetOptions{masterWeight, lowThreshold, medThreshold, highThreshold} for threshold changes], ext = 0}})). Inside: the network id, the account, the sequence number, the fee and the time bounds. Not inside: any other signature. Attached as a DecoratedSignature: a 4-byte hint (the last 4 bytes of the signer's public key) and the 64-byte signature.

steps.does: One member attaches the signatures (at most 20) and submits through the RPC. The RPC provider sees the signed transaction first; validators see it before it is in a ledger. The account pays the fee.

The ledger closes. The new signer set and thresholds are public. Every other proposal collected on this account is now stale by sequence number, and a removed signer's signature no longer counts. Muster would re-read the account, record the read, and re-grade the room's pending proposals.

refusals.why: the chain does not check it: SetOptions writes weights and thresholds as given, and a threshold above the total weight can never be met again, so the account is locked for that operation class

actions.name: Cancel collected transactions by bumping the sequence number
actions.summary: Members void every collected but unsubmitted transaction from the account at once: a BumpSequence operation raises the account's sequence number to at least the highest pending one, so none of them can ever apply. It needs only the LOW threshold. The other route is expiry: a transaction past its timeBounds.maxTime is dead anyway.

fields.means: the new sequence number: at least the highest seqNum among the pending transactions, below INT64_MAX

steps.does: Writes bumpTo at or above the highest seqNum among the account's pending proposals in the room, and lists them. Signers sign until the weights reach LOW. When LOW is below MEDIUM, fewer signers can cancel than can pay. Muster would stop at exactly enough weight.

steps.does: One member submits through the RPC. The RPC provider sees the signed transaction first; validators see it before it is in a ledger.
